title: Esoteric Foundations
tagline: The Western esoteric current, studied as documented history.
blurb: IL-01 is the esoteric academy: Hermetic foundations (the Corpus, the Golden Dawn, Wicca and Thelema, chaos magic, Hermetic Qabalah, alchemy), John Dee and the Enochian system (the documented life, the alphabet, the Angelical Keys, the Monas Hieroglyphica, scholarly reception), and the CCRU seminar (Land, hyperstition, the numogram, meme chaos-magic, Project Cybersyn). Every claim carries its epistemic tier — DOCUMENTED, SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS, TRADITIONAL, or CONTESTED. Assessments test literacy, never belief.

arc.title: The tiers
arc.body: The epistemic discipline first: DOCUMENTED, SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS, TRADITIONAL, CONTESTED. Every text you'll read gets tiered. This is the method that makes the rest honest.

modules.title: Hermetic Foundations
modules.summary: The Western esoteric current from Alexandria to the present: the Hermetic Corpus (Corpus Hermeticum, Asclepius, Nag Hammadi context, late-antique Alexandria), the Golden Dawn (1888–1903 order history, grade system, the LBRP as study object), Wicca and Thelema (Gardnerian origins, Crowley/A.'.A.'/O.T.O., the Book of the Law), chaos magic and Discordianism (Spare's sigilization, Carroll's paradigm shifting, the Principia), Hermetic Qabalah (the Tree of Life, correspondences, tarot), alchemy (Alexandrian roots, Paracelsus, laboratory vs spiritual readings) — all read through the four epistemic tiers.
objectives: Tier claims: DOCUMENTED vs SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS vs TRADITIONAL vs CONTESTED.
Read the Hermetic Corpus in its Alexandrian context.
Trace the Golden Dawn's papers: what they actually say.
Compare laboratory and spiritual readings of alchemy.

notes.title: The Corpus and Alexandria
notes.body:
The **Corpus Hermeticum** and **Asclepius**: dialogues attributed to Hermes Trismegistus — the **Nag Hammadi context** (the 1945 find reframed the texts' world), **late-antique Alexandria** (the syncretic city: Greek philosophy, Egyptian religion, emerging Christianity).

**DOCUMENTED tier evidence**: the manuscript tradition, Casaubon's 1614 dating (the texts are late-antique, not primeval — philology as debunking).

- Alexandria: the crossroads — the Corpus is what happens when Greek, Egyptian, and Jewish thought share a city
- Casaubon's dating: the founding act of esoteric historiography — texts have dates, dates have consequences
- Read the Asclepius first — it's the most complete single Hermetic text

notes.title: The Golden Dawn and its heirs
notes.body:
**Order history 1888–1903**: the Cipher Manuscripts, Westcott/Mathers/Woodman, the schisms. **Grade system and curriculum**: the ladder 0=0 through the grades — study as a curriculum, not a mystery.

**The LBRP as study object**: the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram — read the papers, note what they say vs. what later books claim (**DOCUMENTED tier**: the papers actually say).

**Wicca and Thelema**: Gardnerian Wicca's origins and claims; **Crowley, A.'.A.'., O.T.O.**; the **Book of the Law** as primary text — **TRADITIONAL vs CONTESTED tiering** applied throughout.

- The Cipher Manuscripts: DOCUMENTED as artifacts, CONTESTED as to origin — tier each claim separately
- Grade papers: read them as a curriculum designer would — what's taught, in what order, to what end?
- The Book of the Law: primary text first, Crowley's commentaries second, others' opinions last

notes.title: Chaos magic, Qabalah, alchemy
notes.body:
**Chaos magic**: Austin Osman Spare's **sigilization**, Peter Carroll's **paradigm shifting**; **Discordianism** and the **Principia Discordia** — **belief as instrument** (the chaos-magical move: belief is a tool, not a truth-claim).

**Hermetic Qabalah**: the **Tree of Life as a map**, **correspondences** (planets, elements, tarot), **tarot as a study instrument** — **TRADITIONAL tier**: the transmission story, honestly labeled.

**Alchemy**: **Alexandrian roots**, **Paracelsus and iatrochemistry** (alchemy as early chemistry/medicine), **laboratory vs spiritual readings** — **DOCUMENTED tier**: the textual record.

- Sigilization: the technique is documented; the mechanism is CONTESTED — tier them separately
- Correspondences: a memory palace, whatever else they are — the Tree organizes information
- Paracelsus: 'the dose makes the poison' — alchemy's most DOCUMENTED contribution to science

notes.title: The four epistemic tiers
notes.body:
**DOCUMENTED**: primary sources, artifacts, dated texts — the bedrock. **SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS**: what historians agree on (provisional, cited). **TRADITIONAL**: what lineages claim about themselves — reported, not endorsed. **CONTESTED**: open questions, rival readings, live debates.

**Assessments test literacy, never belief**: you will be asked what the texts say, what the tiers are, and how scholars argue — never what you believe.

- Tier every claim you meet — the reflex is the whole method
- TRADITIONAL ≠ false: it means 'claimed by the lineage' — report it accurately, label it honestly
- CONTESTED is where the seminar lives — the open questions are the interesting ones

cards.back: DOCUMENTED, SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS, TRADITIONAL, CONTESTED.
Primary sources, artifacts, dated texts — the bedrock.

Dated the Corpus Hermeticum to late antiquity — philology as debunking.

choices: CONTESTED on origins; DOCUMENTED on the manuscript date
quiz.explain: Tier each claim separately — the manuscript's date is DOCUMENTED; the origin story is CONTESTED.

quiz.explain: 1614: the texts are late-antique, not primeval — dates have consequences.

quiz.q: The Cipher Manuscripts: origin story is?
quiz.explain: Artifacts: DOCUMENTED. Their origin story: CONTESTED. Separate tiers.

choices: chaos magic's move: belief as tool, not truth-claim
quiz.explain: Paradigm shifting — the chaos-magical technique, tiered as practice not metaphysics.
Whatever else: a memory palace organizing planets, elements, tarot.

modules.title: Dee and the Enochian System
modules.summary: John Dee's documented life (1527–1608/09: court mathematician, navigator, advisor; the Mortlake library), the Enochian alphabet (21 letters, received 6 May 1583), the Angelical Keys (the 48/49 Calls, the 1581/82–1589 diaries, Kelly and Dee's scrying), the Monas Hieroglyphica (1564: the glyph as synthesis of geometry, alchemy, astronomy), and scholarly reception (Casaubon's True and Faithful Relation, Yates and the modern recovery, current scholarship) — praxis as literacy: the commonplace book, the tiered reading journal, no belief required.
objectives: Narrate Dee's documented biography: mathematician, navigator, advisor.
Describe the Enochian system's documented components: alphabet, Calls, diaries.
Read the Monas Hieroglyphica as a synthetic glyph.
Summarize the scholarly reception: Casaubon, Yates, current work.

notes.title: The documented life
notes.body:
**1527–1608/09**: the biographical record. **Court mathematician, navigator, advisor** — Dee advised on the calendar, navigation, and imperial imagination ('Brittany' — the British Empire concept has Dee's fingerprints).

**The Mortlake library**: the largest in England — the material base of Dee's work. **DOCUMENTED tier throughout**: dates, letters, library catalogues.

- Dee the mathematician is DOCUMENTED; Dee the magus is the same man — the split is modern
- Mortlake: the library as laboratory — Dee's power was bibliographic before it was anything else
- Read the biography before the diaries — the man before the mystery

notes.title: The Enochian apparatus
notes.body:
The **Enochian alphabet**: 21 letters, **received 6 May 1583** — letterforms and names. **DOCUMENTED: the diaries as evidence** — the records exist; what they record is the question.

The **Angelical Keys**: the **48/49 Calls** — structure and language. The **diaries 1581/82–1589**: the day-by-day record. **Scrying practice: Kelly and Dee** — the working partnership.

**SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS on the record**: the diaries are genuine 16th-century documents; interpretations vary (CONTESTED).

- 6 May 1583: the date is DOCUMENTED — the reception narrative is TRADITIONAL
- Kelly: the scryer — Dee recorded; the division of labor matters for reading the diaries
- The Calls: study the structure (grammar claims) before the content (entity claims)

notes.title: Monas Hieroglyphica and reception
notes.body:
**Monas Hieroglyphica (1564)**: the glyph as synthesis — **geometry, alchemy, and astronomy in one figure**; Dee's theorems; reception history.

**Scholarly reception**: **Casaubon's True and Faithful Relation** (1659 — the hostile edition that preserved the diaries); **Yates and the modern recovery** (the 20th-century rehabilitation); **current scholarship**; **CONTESTED: the open questions**.

- The Monas: read it as a diagram that thinks — one figure, many disciplines
- Casaubon's irony: the debunker preserved what he attacked — hostile transmission is still transmission
- Yates: the 'Hermetic tradition' thesis — SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS with live CONTESTED edges

notes.title: Praxis as literacy
notes.body:
**Reading Dee's corpus end to end** — the discipline is coverage. **Keeping a commonplace book** — the early-modern method: copy, index, cross-reference.

**The tiered reading journal**: every session tiered — what did I read, what tier is it, what's the evidence?

**No belief required**: the course tests whether you can read, tier, and argue — never what you affirm.

- Commonplace method: copy the striking passage, note the tier, add your question
- Coverage beats cherry-picking — read the boring parts; the boring parts are often the DOCUMENTED ones
- The journal is the artifact — it demonstrates the method

cards.back: 1527–1608/09. Court mathematician, navigator, advisor.
Dee's library — largest in England. Bibliographic power.
21 letters, received 6 May 1583 (DOCUMENTED date; reception TRADITIONAL).
1581/82–1589. Genuine 16th-c. documents (SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS).
1564 — the glyph synthesizing geometry, alchemy, astronomy.
1659 hostile edition that preserved the diaries — hostile transmission.
20th-century recovery of Dee — the 'Hermetic tradition' thesis.
Literacy — commonplace book, tiered journal. No belief required.

quiz.explain: Dee advised on the imperial imagination — DOCUMENTED advisory role.
The division of labor: Kelly saw, Dee wrote — it shapes how we read the diaries.
The Angelical Keys: 48 (or 49) Calls — structure first, content second.
1564 — the synthetic glyph, early in Dee's career.
The 1659 hostile edition preserved what it attacked.
Copy the passage, note the tier, add your question — praxis as literacy.

modules.title: The CCRU Seminar: Hyperstition and Cybernetics
modules.summary: Nick Land and the CCRU (who, where, what; the 1990s writings; primary texts in reading order; the archive as artifact), hyperstition (fiction as an engine, the hyperstitional circuit, examples and counter-examples — CONTESTED theory status), the numogram and syzygies (decimal sorcery, working the diagram, reading a technical diagram as a text), meme chaos-magic theory (sigils in the network age, memes as hyperstitional objects, attention as a medium), and Project Cybersyn (Allende's Chile 1971–73, Stafford Beer, the viable system model, the operations room — what was built vs. mythologized).
objectives: Map the CCRU: people, place, texts, in reading order.
Define hyperstition and test it against examples.
Work the numogram as a technical diagram.
Separate Cybersyn's documented build from its mythology.

notes.title: The Land/CCRU corpus
notes.body:
**Nick Land's 1990s writings** — the Warwick years. **The CCRU: who, where, what** — the Cybernetic Culture Research Unit, Warwick University, mid-to-late 1990s: the collective, the texts, the legend.

**Primary texts in reading order** — the seminar's spine. **The archive as artifact** — how the texts survived (websites, samizdat, reissues) is part of the story.

- Reading order matters: the early essays before the later fragments — the thought has a trajectory
- The archive's fragility: web-era texts vanish — the seminar teaches textual survival too
- Land's later work is a separate question — the seminar covers the 1990s corpus

notes.title: Hyperstition and the numogram
notes.body:
**Hyperstition**: **fiction as an engine** — ideas that make themselves real by being believed/circulated; the **hyperstitional circuit** (belief → action → reality → belief); **examples and counter-examples**; **CONTESTED: the theory's status** — provocative framework or mystified feedback loop?

**The numogram and syzygies**: **decimal sorcery** — the numogram diagram; **syzygies and currents**; **working the diagram**; **reading a technical diagram as a text** — what does it claim, what does it show, what tier?

- Hyperstition test: does the idea change behavior before it's 'true'? — that's the circuit
- Counter-examples: failed prophecies — the circuit needs the feedback to close
- The numogram: treat it like an engineering drawing — precise about an imprecise thing

notes.title: Memes, Cybersyn, and the case study
notes.body:
**Meme chaos-magic theory**: **sigils in the network age** (Spare's technique, networked), **memes as hyperstitional objects**, the **chaos-magic lineage**, **attention as a medium** — the economics of the circuit.

**Project Cybersyn**: **Allende's Chile, 1971–1973**; **Stafford Beer and the viable system model**; **the operations room** (the famous chairs and screens); **what was actually built vs. what is mythologized** — DOCUMENTED build, CONTESTED legacy.

- Memes: hyperstition's mass production — the circuit at internet scale
- Cybersyn DOCUMENTED: the telex network, the VSM design, the ops room — real artifacts
- Cybersyn mythologized: the 'internet before the internet' claims — tier the hype separately
- Beer: management cybernetics — the VSM is the serious theory under the legend

scriptLabs.title: The Tiering Engine
scriptLabs.brief: Build a claim-tiering function: given a claim about an esoteric text, classify it DOCUMENTED / SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS / TRADITIONAL / CONTESTED with a justification. The method as code.
scriptLabs.starter:
def tier_claim(claim, evidence):
    # TODO: return (tier, justification)
    # DOCUMENTED: primary source / artifact / date
    # SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS: historians agree (cite)
    # TRADITIONAL: lineage claims it
    # CONTESTED: open debate
    pass

tests = [
    ('The Corpus Hermeticum manuscripts date to late antiquity', 'Casaubon 1614 philology; manuscript tradition'),
    ('The Golden Dawn was founded by ancient adepts', 'lineage origin story; Cipher MS debate'),
    ('Dee kept angel diaries 1581-1589', 'the diaries exist in archives'),
]
for claim, ev in tests:
    print(tier_claim(claim, ev))
scriptLabs.hint: Keyword routing: 'manuscript/archive/exists' → DOCUMENTED; 'lineage claims/origin story' → TRADITIONAL (or CONTESTED if debated); 'historians agree' → SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS.

scriptLabs.title: Corpus Concordance Builder
scriptLabs.brief: Build a tiny concordance: index key terms across three Hermetic passages, then report which terms co-occur. Textual analysis, the old-fashioned way, with code.
scriptLabs.starter:
passages = {
    'asclepius': 'god is the glory of all things and the divine is the principle of all that is',
    'poimandres': 'the light was the mind of god and the mind encompassed all things',
    'emerald': 'as above so below and as below so above for the miracle of the one thing',
}
# TODO: for each passage, set of significant words (len>3, not stopwords)
# TODO: print pairwise intersections (shared vocabulary)
scriptLabs.hint: stopwords={'the','and','for','was','all','are','that','with'}. sig(p)={w for w in p.split() if len(w)>3 and w not in stopwords}.

scriptLabs.title: The Numogram Walker
scriptLabs.brief: Model the numogram's decimal zone as a graph: digits 0-9 with the syzygy pairings as edges. Walk it, find cycles. Reading a diagram as data.
scriptLabs.starter:
# syzygy pairings (documented structure of the diagram)
pairs = [(0,9),(1,8),(2,7),(3,6),(4,5)]
# TODO: build adjacency for digits 0-9: each digit connects to its pair AND to (d+1)%10 (the decimal circuit)
# TODO: BFS from 0; print distances. Find: does every digit reach every other?
scriptLabs.hint: adj[d] = {pair[d], (d+1)%10, (d-1)%10}. BFS with a deque or list-queue.

scenarios.title: The Tiering Dispute
scenarios.context: A forum claims: 'The Golden Dawn's rituals come from ancient Egypt — it's DOCUMENTED.' You respond.

options.why: Tradition saying so makes it TRADITIONAL, not DOCUMENTED.

options.text: Tier it: the 1888–1903 papers are DOCUMENTED; the Egyptian origin is TRADITIONAL/CONTESTED — separate claims, separate tiers
options.why: The method: tier each claim separately. Papers documented; origins contested.

steps.prompt: They reply: 'Casaubon was wrong.' Your standard?

options.why: Argument without evidence standards is noise.

options.text: Ask for the tier: what primary evidence, what scholarly consensus, what's contested — then read it
options.why: The tier discipline turns disputes into research programs.

options.why: Honest briefing: separate build from myth, theory from furniture.

answerBank.q: Do I have to believe any of this?
answerBank.a: No — assessments test literacy, never belief. The tier system exists precisely so you can study claims rigorously without affirming them. Read, tier, argue.

answerBank.q: Why study esotericism in a tech academy?
answerBank.a: Historiography, primary-source literacy, and the tier discipline transfer everywhere — including to evaluating technical claims. Plus: the history of computing (Dee, cybernetics) runs through this material.

answerBank.q: Isn't the CCRU just internet mysticism?
answerBank.a: The seminar treats it as texts with a documented context (Warwick, 1990s) and a CONTESTED theory (hyperstition). Read the corpus, tier the claims, argue the status — that's the work.
The Asclepius (complete, short), then Dee's biography, then the Land/CCRU corpus in reading order. Commonplace book from day one.
It's the assessment artifact: every reading logged with tier, evidence, and your open question. It demonstrates the method — which is the actual skill being taught.

answerBank.q: How do TRADITIONAL claims get treated?
answerBank.a: Reported accurately, labeled honestly — never endorsed, never mocked. 'The lineage claims X' is a DOCUMENTED fact about the claim, whatever X's own tier is.
